newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM to protect rights of opposition leader.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM to protect rights of opposition leader.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Thursday pledged to protect the legal rights of opposition leader Sam Rainsy following speculation that courts planned to question him in a murder case.
"I must protect Sam Rainsy, protect him in his capacity as a citizen...everything must be in conformity with the law," Norodom said.
The prince was responding to rumours that the Phnom Penh Municipal Court planned to summon the Khmer Nation Party (KNP) leader for questioning in the murder of co-Premier Hun Sen's brother-in-law.
Kov Samuth was shot dead outside a Phnom Penh restaurant on November 19 in what has been widely viewed as a political killing.
Court officials were unavailable for comment. Sam Rainsy left on a trip to Australia on Wednesday, due to return on March 22.
The court on March 3 charged KNP security chief and steering committee member Srun Vong Vannak and two other men with involvement in the slaying.

During a protest in Phnom Penh on Wednesday, opposition members demanded Srun Vong Vannak be released and given access to legal counsel. The party says he is innocent and that his February 14 arrest was engineered by Hun Sen, a bitter foe of the KNP, in a bid to destabilise the party.
The KNP recently formed an alliance with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, the main partner and rival of Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party in the uneasy coalition government formed in 1993.
Ranariddh told reporters he had asked the justice and interior ministries to investigate the case thoroughly but could not comment before receiving a full report.
But he said Sam Rainsy's legal rights must be respected and he would oppose any attempt to violate them.
